explanation: Nori sheets are made much like paper: the seaweed is chopped, spread thinly on frames and dried, a method adapted from Japanese papermaking in the Edo period.

claims.text: Nori, dried in thin sheets, is the seaweed used to wrap sushi rolls.
Kombu, wakame and hijiki are other edible seaweeds not used as sushi wrappers.
Nori sheets are made by chopping the seaweed, spreading it on frames and drying it, as paper is made.
The sheet method for nori was adapted from Japanese papermaking during the Edo period.
